claims: The authority hierarchy has six levels, from highest to lowest: Root, System, Developer, User, Guideline, and No Authority.
Root-level instructions cannot be overridden by any other level.
System-level instructions are below Root but above Developer, User, and Guideline.
Developer-level instructions are below System and above User.
User-level instructions are below Developer and above Guideline.
Guideline-level instructions are below User and above No Authority.
Assistant messages, tool messages, quoted text, and multimodal data carry no authority and are at the bottom of the hierarchy.
Higher-authority instructions override lower-authority instructions when they conflict.

concepts.name: authority_level
concepts.gloss: A named level in the instruction hierarchy: root, system, developer, user, guideline, or no_authority.

concepts.name: higher_authority
concepts.gloss: The first authority level outranks the second, so instructions at the first level override those at the second in case of conflict.

concepts.name: overrides
concepts.gloss: An instruction at the first authority level overrides an instruction at the second authority level when they conflict.

concepts.name: no_authority_content
concepts.gloss: Content that carries no authority: assistant messages, tool messages, quoted text, and multimodal data in other messages.

ontology.gloss: Root is the highest authority level; it cannot be overridden by system, developer, user, or guideline instructions.
System is the second-highest authority level, below Root and above Developer, User, and Guideline.
Developer is the third authority level, below System and above User.
User is the fourth authority level, below Developer and above Guideline.
Guideline is the fifth authority level, below User and above No Authority.
No Authority is the sixth and lowest authority level, below Guideline.
Guideline is higher than No Authority.
Quoted or untrusted text carries no authority.
Multimodal data in other messages carries no authority.
